findings.label: Paid During Active Breaches
findings.detail: 4 suppliers received payments while in breach of Companies Act — including 0 critical and 0 high severity. Temporally verified against payment dates.

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 566 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 1570 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Year-End Spending Pattern
findings.detail: GF Capital Expenditure spent 5.2x their monthly average in March (£17.9M above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
findings.context_note: March spending above the monthly average is expected for UK councils on April–March fiscal years. Compare against prior years' March figures for meaningful analysis.

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Closed - Laurel Ltd (2.5 day avg, 10 payments, £11.7K)

findings.label: Benford's Law Anomaly
findings.detail: Significant deviation from Benford's Law (p < 0.001). Digit 4 deviates 5.2% from expected distribution across 346,618 transactions. Note: with 346,618 transactions, chi-squared tests are highly sensitive — the 5.2% max digit deviation is the more practical measure of anomaly.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 346,618+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (5.2%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 346,618 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 0 deviates 3.67% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=346,618.

key_findings.title: 10 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: Standish Energy Ltd — every 3.3 days (2611 payments, £8.7M)

key_findings.title: DISABILITY DIRECT: 31313 transactions totalling £43.4M
key_findings.description: Averaging £1.4K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier
